sections.title: Context
sections.body: Koa Health was a digital mental health company (Series B, ~150 people) with a product portfolio targeting clinically diagnosed conditions. This project was developed at Telefonica R&D in collaboration with Hospital Clinic Barcelona and O2 UK. The team comprised product, data science, engineering, and clinical partners. I led product and service design.

sections.title: Problem
sections.body: Psychiatrists had no reliable way to monitor patients between appointments. Patients with bipolar disorder often lack insight into their own mood state — particularly during manic episodes — making self-reporting unreliable. Clinicians were flying blind between clinical contacts, and deteriorations were only caught when they became crises. The business problem was demonstrating clinical utility to unlock commercial partnerships with health systems.

sections.title: My role
sections.body: I led product and service design across data science, clinical, and engineering teams. I personally owned the clinical use case definition with Hospital Clinic, the design of the clinician-facing interface, and the translation of model outputs into clinically meaningful information. Data science and engineering work was delegated.

sections.title: Approach
sections.body: The core insight was that changes in bipolar state are reflected in behavioural signals already passively captured by mobile networks: call patterns, data usage, location history, sleep-wake cycles. I worked with data scientists to identify which signals tracked reliably with clinical mood state, then designed the clinician dashboard around nursing and psychiatric workflows rather than the raw model output. A deliberate decision was made to operate at the network level — not via a smartphone app — to ensure coverage across the full patient population, including older patients and those who might change devices during an episode.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.body:
The service gave psychiatrists a continuous, objective view of patient state between appointments, replacing a gap that previously required expensive wearables or frequent patient-initiated check-ins. Clinical partners at Hospital Clinic validated the approach. The project contributed to Telefonica's health portfolio and informed subsequent work on bipolar-related monitoring at Koa Health.

Quantified clinical outcome metrics were not published externally for this project.
